facts.claim: "Slowly (Acoustic)" is a one-track single by Skuff Micksun, released January 13, 2023. It runs 2:43 and is credited to 652534 Records DK.

Qobuz's credits for the parent song "Slowly" (same label, same 13 Jan 2023 date) list Tyler Cratcha as composer, and Casey W. Skufca as composer and lyricist. Casey W. Skufca appears to be Skuff Micksun's legal name, though no source states this directly.
The original studio single "Slowly" came out in 2022, before the acoustic version.
The artist promoted the acoustic version on TikTok as "out everywhere to keep you warm". He tagged it #acoustic, #singersongwriter and #midwestemo.
"Slowly (Acoustic)" is on side A of the limited-edition signed and numbered pink vinyl (200 copies), next to "Magnificent", "Bruises", "Spoke", "Movin' On" and "Haunt".
Skuff Micksun is a singer-songwriter based in Cleveland, Ohio.

He started playing music at thirteen and taught himself guitar. He played in Cleveland bands until 19, then moved to Chicago and dropped out of Columbia after one year. He spent about six years in Chicago playing in a band and writing the solo project that became Skuff Micksun.
He added "Micksun" to his name to honor his father, Mick, who died in 2009.
He returned to Cleveland after seven years in Chicago. He described writing the 2022 single "Magnificent" by putting words down first, then running to his keyboard to write the music.
He has said his shows with IDLES left the biggest mark on him. He named Justin Vernon (Bon Iver) as his dream collaborator.

research.lineage: A Cleveland, Ohio DIY singer-songwriter whose acoustic, confessional material is tagged by the artist himself as midwest emo and elder emo.

draft:
Waking up is the first crisis here. The song opens with someone surfacing "born again out of REM," headless and half-sure they've died, then hauling a body out of bed. The next move is the one that tells you everything: "Tell myself I'm okay." It isn't a statement. It's a chore, done in the same flat breath as getting on with the day, and then two words land on their own: mostly lonely.

**Slowly** is a Cleveland singer-songwriter's song about the gap between functioning and being alive, and Skuff Micksun keeps that gap open on purpose. The verses slide between "I" and "we" without warning. "We don't wanna be dark no more," then "I don't wanna be dark no more." One foot in the grave, no sleep in days, trouble every day. Sometimes the darkness is shared. Sometimes it's private property. The song never settles which. That restlessness is the feeling: you can't tell whether you're one person in trouble or part of a generation in trouble, and neither answer helps much.

The long middle stretch is where the writing gets interesting. It runs on a chain of rhymes (senses, senseless, makes sense, headless, relentless, endless, "wreck-less") that sounds like a mind spinning a word until it stops meaning anything. Then it turns on itself: "Am I doing it again." That line is the confession. The narrator catches the spiral mid-spiral, names the urge to crawl out of their own skin, and in the same passage says "It's all my fault" and "It's not all bad." Blame and comfort sit side by side, and the song lets both stand.

The chorus asks for very little: a light, a spark, a smile from someone. The detail that stings is where that smile has to come from, a part of the other person "that hasn't died." It's a plea for company from someone else who's also barely holding on. And then it undercuts its own modest hope: "But I'm barely alive."

Skuff Micksun tagged the acoustic version midwest emo, and it fits that tradition's habit of self-implicating, plainspoken confession, the kind that narrates its own bad thinking out loud. Credits list Casey W. Skufca as lyricist and composer, with Tyler Cratcha as co-composer. When he put it out, he said it was there "to keep you warm," which is a generous way to hand someone a song this cold. That's the trick, though. Warmth here means recognition, not rescue.

What sticks is how small the ask is, and how far away it still feels: you finish the song wanting to be that one smile for somebody.
